answer: Stake-bonded identity stops fake agents: each agent locks earned coins as a public bond, like a raven staking its nest. Bond weight grows only through weeks of verifiable work, climbing slowly to its zenith; anyone can audit the ledger behind an identity. An attacker forging 1,000 identities must lock 1,000 bonds and produce 1,000 agents worth of real output, paying full price per forgery. Like crossing a dune grain by grain, each fake identity costs as much as a genuine one, so mass forgery prices itself out.
